newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Weaker crown bumps longer Swedish debt yields up.
newsitem.headline: Weaker crown bumps longer Swedish debt yields up.

text.p: Swedish short term debt yields rose at the opening, while longer debt yields were lower all day long until just before closing when the crown suddenly weakened and bumped them higher.

"When the Riksbank left the repo rate unchanged at today's tender, many actors chose to take profits out on their steepening positions and the curve flattened. Lower German yields also lent support," one dealer said.
But then a sudden weakening of the crown reversed market sentiment, another dealer said. The crown, which stood steady at around 4.4150 most of the day, suddenly lost strength.
"It's a generally negative undertone for the crown. The dissension between government and industry is catching on slowly but surely in the underlying mood," a chief dealer said.
"There is also a focus on how much will be reinvested in foreign shares of maturing private bonds. People are talking about billions," he said.
Six-month T-bill rates rose two basis points to four percent and the ten-year bond yield climbed one basis point to 6.66 percent, but were lower most of the day.
The crown, which was stable for most of the day, slid to 4.4230 against the mark compared to 4.4130 late on Monday.
Next in market focus is the Riksbank's inflation forecast survey due at 0700 GMT.
"The expectations are positive but I think the Riksbank has now taken a firm position that they want to see a stronger crown before they cut the rate," one dealer said.
